customManagers.description: Track GitHub Actions wrapped by Wandalen/wretry.action. Renovate's github-actions manager only reads `uses:`, not the nested `action:` input wretry takes, so without this the retry-wrapped actions (setup-buildx, checkout, login, …) would silently stop receiving updates.

packageRules.description: Group all GitHub Actions bumps into one PR.

nginx + supervisor are pinned in the Dockerfile and tracked via the `deb` datasource (markers there). Repology strips the Debian -N+debNNuM revision so it can't see security rebuilds; the deb datasource reads the actual package index. Point it at both trixie (base) and trixie-security so security revisions are picked up — Renovate merges the registries and takes the highest. All apt bumps grouped into one PR.
Standalone bumps for tool versions tracked in build.yml (crane, etc.).
Major bumps require manual review — surface as checkboxes on the Dependency Dashboard, do not open the PR automatically, do not auto-merge. Minor/patch still flow through automerge gated by all-ci.

Keep GitHub Actions on floating major tags (@vN), including the wretry-wrapped `action:` inputs the custom regex manager tracks. Suppress pin/patch/minor so they are never pinned to an exact patch (GitHub moves the @vN tag, so patch fixes land at runtime without a PR); a new MAJOR still surfaces via the rule above. This matches how the unwrapped `uses:` actions already behave and stops the one-PR-per-action churn the regex manager would otherwise create.

Exempt wretry.action from the floating-major suppression above. Unlike the wrapped actions it is exact-pinned (it executes arbitrary nested actions, so we want reviewed updates, not a moving tag), so it must keep receiving patch/minor bump PRs — e.g. a future Node 24 release that clears the runner's node20-deprecation warning. Without this, the rule above would freeze it at v3.8.0 until a new MAJOR.
